questions.question:
**In the given sentence identify the segment which contains a grammatical error.**

There are some members who haven't paid his subscription yet.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'his subscription yet'.** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The erroneous part **'his subscription yet' **should be **'their subscription yet'.** 
 
• We know that **'his'** is used when **the noun it is referring to is singular.** 
 
• In the given question, **'some members'** is **plural.** Therefore, a plural form of the possessive pronoun,** 'their'** should be used. 
 
• Here, **'his'** will be changed into** 'their'. **
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4.** 

 ​

**Correct Answer:__** *There are some members who haven't paid **their subscription yet. ***** **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• Some verbs are proceeded by **reflexive Pronoun:**

 
 
• **Average, Revenge, Present, Absent, Pride, Available, Acquit, Reconcile, Apply, etc. **
 
• Example: The IAF's Canberra bomber squadrons too acquitted themselves__ better than their PAF counterparts with their daring strikes deep inside Pakistani territory. 
 
 
 
• If we use* *an intransitive verb in a sentence then there is no need for a Direct object/ Reflexive Pronoun/ Verbs which we usually do for ourselves. Such kinds of '**Verbs**' are:
 
 
• Complain, Shave, Shower, Keep, Stop, Behave, Pit, Remember, Down, etc.
 
 
• Example: *Justin always shaves on Sunday. *

• The given sentence is an example of Sentence Jumble. 
 
• The first statement of a sentence jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, the starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'.
 
• In the given sentence,** Part C **will be the first sentence because it is **an independent general statement.** We know that it is one of **the most common drinks in Asia. **
 
• **Part A** will be the next sentence because it tells us **the process of making tea. **
 
• The next sentence will be **Part B** because **Part A and Part B** are connected. **Part B **further tells about **tea making.** 
 
• Lastly, **Part D **will be used. 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4. **​

questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

Mother said to Avika, "Finish these sums before you go to the park."

options.text: Mother told Avika to finish those sums before she goes to the park.
Mother told Avika to finish these sums before you go to the park.
Mother told Avika to finish those sums before she went to the park.
Mother told Avika to finish those sums before she was going to the park.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Mother told Avika to finish those sums before she went to the park.'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in **Direct Speech.** As per the given question, we have to change it into **Indirect Speech.** 
 
• The process of transformation is as follows: 
 
 
• **'Said to' **will be changed into **'told'** because **the reporting verb has an object. **
 
• The given sentence is an example of **an imperative sentence. **
 
• Transformation of Imperative Sentence. 
 
• 'Orders', 'Command', 'Request', 'Advice' are given in these kinds of sentences. 
 
• Reporting Verb is changed into 'ordered, advised, requested, commanded, beg, forbade, suggested, proposed, assured, asked, reminded, warned, agreed, refused, promised', etc. 
 
• Inverted Commas will be removed. And conjunction 'to/not to' will be used. 
 
• *Example: *
 
 
• *He said, "Mohan, please bring me my towel." (Direct Speech)*
 
• *He requested Mohan to bring him his towel. (Indirect Speech)*
 
 
 
• **'To'** will be used as a conjunction. 
 
• **'These'** will be changed into** 'those'. **
 
• **'You'** will be changed into** 'she'.** We know that **the second person pronoun** is changed according to **the object of the reporting verb. **
 
• **'Go' **will be changed into **'went'. **
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3. **

 ​

**Indirect speech:__** *Mother told Avika to finish those sums before she went to the park.*
